projects.title: Polymer Lithography Simulation
projects.one: Block copolymer phase separation, simulated to guide the lab.
projects.ctx: RIT Honors research, Dr. Padmanabhan. LAMMPS.
projects.designed: The same system settles into holes, spheres, stripes, or lamellae depending on chemistry. Which pattern you get is the design space.
projects.analyzed: About 100 lines of molecular dynamics with the Weeks-Chandler-Andersen potential, run in LAMMPS on the RIT cluster across thousands of cases.
projects.built: The build is the simulation itself. No physical rig.
projects.proved: The runs reached clean separated end states; the interaction parameter falls with temperature and rises with repulsion, a starting map for the lab.

projects.title: Additive Manufacturing and Investment Casting
projects.one: Molten aluminium into a printed ceramic mold.
projects.ctx: RIT, AMPrint Center. Fusion 360, nTopology, CFD.
projects.designed: Negative mold in Fusion 360, pour holes up top and drains at the bottom, tilted 2 degrees so a 90 degree overhang stayed printable; a truncated-octahedron lattice in nTopology keeps the shell from warping.
projects.analyzed: Transient CFD with air and liquid aluminium at 1273 K, checking for an early freeze or trapped air.
projects.built: The mold prints and the pour is designed. No clean photo of the finished cast nozzle yet.
projects.proved: The CFD showed a complete fill before any metal was melted. You find the cold shut on the screen, not in a ruined mold.
projects.key: Molten aluminium into a printed ceramic mold.

projects.title: PrintNC Build, CNC Router
projects.one: A steel CNC router I built on the third floor of an apartment.
projects.designed: Worked from the PrintNC reference in Fusion 360, sized for the cut area I wanted.
projects.analyzed: Rigidity is in the steel. The spindle and its VFD needed an EMI line filter, shielded cabling, and a star ground away from the logic.
projects.built: Welded steel frame, assembled gantry, water-cooled spindle, wired and running.
projects.proved: It cuts. The first pass was rough, the second came out with clean vertical walls, and it now cuts parts for other projects.

projects.title: 3D Slicer and G-code Generator
projects.one: I wrote the thing that tells my printer what to do.
projects.designed: A small pipeline that exposes every stage: load an STL, set layer height and resolution, slice, generate.
projects.analyzed: Every layer is computed and drawn, so I can see the wall paths and check geometry at each height.
projects.built: The working program slices a real STL and writes G-code end to end.
projects.proved: It generates usable G-code from an arbitrary STL. It is the base for research on tilted and curved slicing planes.
projects.key: STL to G-code, written from scratch.

projects.title: 3D Printing and Fabrication
projects.one: A hand-wound electric motor that spins, and overheats.
projects.ctx: Personal, started at RIT. FDM, PLA and PETG.
projects.designed: An electric motor from scratch, printed stator and rotor, copper wound by hand around the teeth.
projects.analyzed: The prototype runs but overheats: load-bearing parts are PLA that softens under heat. The fix is PETG or PA-CF. That's the finding.
projects.built: Stator wound by hand, motor assembled on its bearing; the same practice produced a MagSafe stand and an Iron Man helmet.
projects.proved: The motor spins, proving the geometry and the winding. The MagSafe stand costs about 4 dollars of PLA against a 69 dollar store version.
projects.key: About 4 dollars of PLA against a 69 dollar store version.

projects.title: Double Pendulum Experiment
projects.one: Model and rig agree for about a second and a half.
projects.designed: A Lagrangian model of the two-arm pendulum, integrated as ODEs in MATLAB.
projects.analyzed: The rig captured at 120 fps, dots tracked in Kinovea; a Monte Carlo envelope from 1000 runs sets the band.
projects.built: Two solid arms on bearings, top arm released from 45 degrees against a hard stopper.
projects.proved: Model and rig agree for about a second and a half; the disagreement after quantifies the bearing friction and imperfect release.
projects.key: Agreement for about 1.5 seconds, then chaos.

projects.title: Vacuum Cannon Experiment
projects.designed: A 1.52 m PVC pipe sealed at both ends, a vacuum pump, and a ballistic block that records displacement.
projects.analyzed: Exit velocity recovered with an Eulerian method integrating the net pressure force, using a Vena Contracta inlet coefficient.
projects.built: The taped PVC tube and pump. No separate build photo.
projects.proved: Predicted against measured across 10 runs at 2 and 8 kPa; friction is the next physics to add.

projects.title: Flight Dynamics Simulation
projects.one: A quaternion attitude model across nine aircraft.
projects.designed: A quaternion attitude model rather than Euler angles, to avoid gimbal lock and integration singularities.
projects.analyzed: A run applies a stick, rudder, or aileron step and logs the response; nine aircraft through the same conditions.
projects.built: A model, not hardware: the Simulink and MATLAB code that runs the nine configurations.
projects.proved: The logged response curves compare directly against real flight-test data.
projects.key: Nine aircraft through the same step inputs.
